clue.text: Taxi overturned by a cart conveying game

indicators.note: a vehicle that is overturned is upside down, so the word for taxi is read backwards

parts.note: a taxi is a cab

indicators.note: the cart is conveying, that is carrying, the A inside it

explanation.surface: A cab tipped over by a cart that was carrying a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns CAB into BAC; the CART 'conveying' A makes CARAT. 'by' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game played between banker and players.

parts.note: auxiliary verbs in English include be
auxiliary verbs in English also include have

explanation.surface: Performing as stand-ins or supporting troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The two commonest English auxiliary (helping) verbs sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct oneself in a certain way is both to act and to behave.

definitions.meaning: Sydney ... is the hero of Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities
a cardboard box, as for milk or eggs

explanation.definitionFit: A Dickens character's surname is also a cardboard box for goods.

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a peal is a chime of bells

explanation.surface: A soft ringing of bells summoning people.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal is a request or plea, a call for help.

clue.text: Sufficient reason for a politician to use lace trimming

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: trimming here means cutting and rearranging, so the letters of use and lace are reworked

explanation.surface: A politician finds good grounds to wear lace trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimming' looks like it describes lace, but it signals an anagram of USE and LACE, giving LECAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful and cause means grounds, so the phrase is adequate justification.

parts.note: split as over-time: tide (time) turned over, read backwards
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: An extra-hours option offered to a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Overtime' as 'over time': tide, an old word for time (as in Yuletide), turned over gives EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior newspaper worker who prepares copy, a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Draw on defunct form of energy

parts.note: defunct means dead
heat is a form of energy

explanation.surface: Drawing upon some extinct kind of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' is the definition, a tied race, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race finishing level, i.e. a tie.

clue.text: One willing to try and bring back routine

parts.note: to try is to test

indicators.note: bringing a word back means reading it from end to start

parts.note: a rota is a routine schedule of duties

explanation.surface: Someone keen to attempt to restore a set routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person making a will, so one who is 'willing' in the legal sense.

parts.note: red is a colour
start means origin or beginning

explanation.surface: A bird whose beginnings were bright.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail.

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument
a pipe is a wind instrument

explanation.surface: A dance performed to the music of two instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance associated with sailors.

clue.text: Assembled in sound part of ship

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for a part of a ship is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: the mast is the upright spar of a ship

explanation.surface: Gathered together in a solid section of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'sturdy', but it is the cue for a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Massed means gathered into a body, i.e. brought together in a crowd.

parts.note: the viola is a stringed instrument
Edward 'Ted' Heath was British Prime Minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: Was a musical instrument damaged by the former Prime Minister?
explanation.definitionFit: Violated means broken or desecrated, so spoiled or damaged.

definitions.meaning: to cross someone is to frustrate or oppose them
a rower's seat set across a boat

explanation.surface: A seat in the House of Lords for independent peers.
explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate a plan, and a seat running across a rowing boat.

clue.text: Part of body that goes very soft in water

indicators.note: the very soft marking goes in, inside the name for water

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular name for water
PP is pianissimo, the musical direction for very soft

explanation.surface: A body part that becomes mushy when soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is old slang for water, the first man's only drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the bulge of cartilage at the front of the throat.

clue.text: Make difficult work of a sentence

parts.note: hard means difficult
labour means work

explanation.surface: Making a job harder than it needs to be over a grammatical sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks grammatical, but here it is a judicial punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour was a prison punishment of compulsory heavy toil handed down by courts.

indicators.note: the word for when is set in, placed inside, the word for mortar

parts.note: cement is a mortar
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A window put into place with mortar.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged window that opens like a door.

clue.text: Ill-conceived article about first navigational instrument

indicators.note: the jumbled article goes about, around, the letter taken from navigational
something ill-conceived is badly put together, so the letters are rearranged
first means only the opening letter of navigational is used

explanation.surface: A badly thought-out item on the earliest navigation device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-conceived' rearranges ARTICLE into CLARIET, which goes 'about' N.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument.

indicators.note: after places the word for outspoken behind the word for tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
plain can mean frank or outspoken

explanation.surface: A vicar speaking bluntly once tea is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a priest attached to an institution such as a regiment or college.
The phrase means both identical in every case and 'even so'.

indicators.note: agonised means twisted in pain, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird gives an anguished scream.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrike or butcher-bird is a songbird that impales prey on thorns.

clue.text: Man put on island by Trojan queen

indicators.note: put on, in a down clue, places the first piece above the second

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, standing for a man
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A man was exiled to an island by the queen of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecuba was wife of King Priam of Troy in Greek legend.

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
end means finish

explanation.surface: Watching the end of a race as a spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' belongs in the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be there in person.

indicators.note: letters in ecstasy are beside themselves, so they are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother or father overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ecstasy' is both the meaning and the signal to rearrange PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrapt means carried away with delight, i.e. rapturous.

clue.text: Hats ordered by county town of Uzbekistan

indicators.note: ordered means put in a fresh sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: Headgear requested by a provincial Central Asian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'requested' but rearranges HATS into TASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital and largest city of Uzbekistan.

clue.text: Nine want vacillating dean to support measure

indicators.note: to support means to come behind, holding up, the printer's measure

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering back and forth, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nine people need a wavering dean to back a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a group or set of nine.

clue.text: Natural ability tied up at outset

indicators.note: read as out-set, set out afresh, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Talent constrained from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outset' seems to mean the start, but read as 'set out' it signals an anagram of TIED UP AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitude is an innate talent or flair.

indicators.note: letters put at risk are thrown about and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is safe from the giants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risk' rearranges the letters of ISN'T AT; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were a race of giant elder gods in Greek myth.

clue.text: Watchful hero encountering drawback at this place

parts.note: here means at this place

indicators.note: back means the word draw is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An alert hero meets a drawback here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAW into WARD. Hereward the Wake, an English rebel against William the Conqueror, is 'watchful' because a wake is a vigil.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward, nicknamed the Wake, was a Saxon resistance leader; wakeful means alert.
